title: See How Sweet Domino Park Really Is
summary: Learn about the history of Domino Park, how to get there, and what neighborhoods have apartments to rent in the area.
body_markdown:
Before it gets too cold, make sure to enjoy the fall weather in Domino Park! With over 6 acres of opportunities to relax on the waterfront, Domino Park is a must-visit destination for people this fall! Let’s see the history, directions, and housing opportunities in the area!


## History


In 1856, the Domino Sugar Refinery was responsible for 98% of the sugar production in the United States. The Williamsburg location took the title of the “jewel in the crown” of the company, with its ability to produce 4 million pounds of sugar a day. Thanks to this location providing the output that it could, the surrounding area in Williamsburg finally got the opportunity to grow into what you see today.


In 1950s, due to market crashes, political change, and lack of industrial activity in Brookln, there was a significant drop in production. This would take out business after business, including the Domino Sugar Refinery, which was the last major active industrial operation on the waterfront.


## Current State of the Park


The preservation of the Domino Sugar Refinery serves as a reminder of the history of Domino Sugar. The factory building sits in the center of Domino Park and is one of the landmark sites when driving into Brooklyn over any of the bridges. The yellow neon sign shines bright as the brick façade will be preserved.


The park includes more than 30 historic artifacts that were closely associated with the Domino Sugar Refinery. These components were all related to Domino and the inner workings. Some of the artifacts include


### Mooring Bollards


To secure docked ships on the East River Waterfront, blue mooring bollards sit on the ground. These would be essential to get the raw sugar cane and other supplies to the refinery without the ships floating away!


### Bucket Conveyors


To get the sugar to different parts of the refinery, bucket conveyors play a critical part and are immortalized in the park to show how sugar went from raw to refined.


### Syrup Tanks


There used to 14 large-scale syrup tanks that served the purpose of collecting high volumes of liquid sweetener the refinery would produce. To honor the sweet tanks, four tanks remain to represent the 14.


### Screw Conveyors


Giant screws represent the Screw Conveyors, which were used to move sugar in various forms to different parts of the refinery, just like the bucket conveyors.


### Gantry Cranes


There are two 80-foot tall cranes at the north end of the park. These originally would unload bulk sugarcane from freight ships to store sugar that the Raw Sugar Warehouse.


### Warehouse Columns


21 columns are connected to the Elevated Walkway; they have always been there. The Elevated Walkway was built with the columns where they always were.


## Open Hours and Directions


While the park might not be open all night, it is open for most of the day! Park hours are 6am-11pm. Plenty of time to enjoy the sites!


There at plenty of ways to get to Domino Park by public transit! On the subway, you can take the J, M, or Z trains to Marcy Ave or the L to Bedford. For Buses, hop on the B32 or Q59 and get off at the


Kent Avenue and South 1st Street


stop. The B62 will get you there if you get off at the


Bedford Avenue and South 4th Street stop. You can get off at the Washington Plaza stop if you take any of the following: B24, B39, B44, B46, B54, or the B59.


If you would rather take a Citibike,there are stations at the following locations:


- South 4th Street & Wythe Ave


- South 3rd Street & Bedford Ave


- Wythe Avenue & Metropolitan Ave


- Metropolitan Avenue & Bedford Ave


- Broadway & Berry Street


If you prefer to drive, do not fret! There is


Parking available at 325 Kent Avenue. Entrances are on South 3rd or South 4th Streets between Kent Avenue and Wythe Avenue.


This does differ from the actual address of the park, which is 15 River St. Brooklyn, NY 11249.


If you want to feel like the old workers of the Domino refinery, you can also take the ferry! Just take the NYC Ferry’s East River route to the South Williamsburg or North Williamsburg stop.


So if you are meeting friends and taking different forms of transportation, make sure you know where you are meeting up!


## Rules


Let us all make sure the park is a welcoming place for all and follow the rules listed by the park. Including:


- Amplify sound, or conduct performances or commercial activity


- Solicit or distribute materials


- Smoke or use drugs


- Bring alcohol outside of Tacocina


- Climb any structure or historical artifact


- Enter plant beds and/or pick flowers


- Use open flames, cook, or grill


- Unleash your dog, except at the dog run


- Fish, feed, and/or abuse wildlife


- Bring additional furniture, including chairs, tables, and tents


- Secure your bike to objects other than bike racks


- Engage in disorderly conduct and inappropriate behavior


- Accompany and monitor your dog at all times


- Pick up after your dog


- Dogs exhibiting aggressive behavior must leave immediately


- Users of the dog run do so at their own risk


- Remember to remind your dog its a good boy or girl.


## Activities


### Ice Skating


Seasonally, there are specific activities available in the Square. This includes ice skating. Even though ice skating at the park is not free, rentals are! You can also bring your own skates if you have them.


### Volleyball


If you want to play volleyball, all you have to do is ask a staff member if you would like to borrow any equipment. There is a one-hour limit, which goes into effect if there are others waiting. If you want to join or start a league, make sure to get a permit from the park. Just to be on the safe side, keep hydrated while playing!


### Bocce


Similar rules to Volleyball, make sure to reach out to the Domino Park staff if you would like to play bocce or need any equipment. Make sure there is no misuse of the court.
